environment: local postgres:16-alpine at 127.0.0.1:55432, same machine for before and after; no hosted/VM access
change: PostgresJsonOwnerStore.insert_if_absent now finds a unique_fields collision with one SQL query (COALESCE(payload->field,'null') = ANY(python-equal json candidates), ORDER BY updated_at, record_id LIMIT 1) instead of SELECT payload of every row. Legacy JSON-string payloads are probed by a string-typed query (partial index, normally zero rows); only if one matches does it fall back to the previous oldest-first pass. An expression index on the compared expressions plus a tiny partial index for string payloads is created lazily (savepoint, once per process, failure falls back to the correct scan).
